short: Pictish warriors used different types of spears, they are depicted with large spearheads. Most of them had throwing darts-for most Celtic tribes javelins were the main offensive weapon, sometimes they were thrown with a strap attached to the shaft. Most of the Picts had no protective armor. The helmet was the chief's privilege, but all the warriors had shields, including their bucklers, of several forms, painted with swirls and spirals. The Picts used small round or square shields. The last were of two kinds: a square shield with an umbon and a square shield with notches at the top and bottom, H-shaped. In some Pictish carvings we see decorated shields, and it is possible that such shields had a covering of stamped leather, could be decorated with copper rivets and shackles. In Pictish carvings it is impossible to identify armor, except for one or two figures, which may show a quilted leather tunic. Helmets are rare; the Aberlemno Sculptured Stones depict riders wearing fairly typical helmets with long nasal plates and cheek pieces, similar to those found in Coppergate and Benty Grange, but these are clearly not Picts. At any case, that is Paul Wagner's opinion, and it has to be respected. The Mordach stone shows us a strange figure who seems to be wearing a helmet with a crest, but to whom it belonged again is unknown.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
